title: SIGIL analysis session v1
description: Schema for the analysis session (`schema: "sigil-session/1"`), SIGIL's source of truth. Self-contained: no external $ref. Strict: additionalProperties: false on every object. Enums are externally tagged with their variant names; struct fields are snake_case. Validation by this schema is necessary but not sufficient: sigil-model's Session::validate checks references and claim invariants the schema cannot express.

ArtifactId.description: Content identity: sha256 of the whole file. Never a path.

SliceId.description: One architecture slice of an artifact: <artifact>#<arch>@<offset>.

ModelId.description: A model in a model store: model:<root id>/<manifest path under manifests/>.

RootId.description: A scan root declared in the request.

FnId.description: A function, unique within its slice's code facts.

CallId.description: A call site, unique within its slice's code facts.

ValueId.description: A process value (one key, one role, one origin).

CondId.description: A condition of a detection rule.

CheckId.description: An audit check whose coverage decides completeness.

ObligationId.description: A profile obligation or profile code check.

PremiseId.description: Something a claim depends on that is not established (shares the ID space of obligations).

RuleId.description: A detection rule that yields findings or open questions.

ProfileRuleId.description: A rule inside a semantic profile.

ProfileRef.description: A semantic profile at a revision: <id>@<revision>. Its hash is in `knowledge`.

ComponentKey.description: A component name used by identification.

ProcessRole.description: A process role from a topology rule. Generic: no runtime-specific meaning.

AtomName.description: A profile-named operand of a predicate check.

PolicyRuleRef.description: The policy rule a decision came from.

AnalyzerRef.description: The analyzer that derived a fact.

UntrustedText.description: Input-derived text. A string when valid UTF-8; otherwise {"hex": <lowercase hex of the bytes>}, used only for values that are not valid UTF-8. Consumers must escape it before display.

Session.description: One analysis run: the source of truth. Exports are derived from it.

SessionExcerpt.description: Part of a session, for documentation examples: every top-level field is optional; inner types are complete.

model_filter.description: Only the model with this display name is inventoried (exact match); null for all.

ObservationMeta.description: When and as whom the run happened. Not part of analysis.

Model.description: One model in a model store: facts only. Whether a blob is missing, malformed, unread, or mismatched is derived from the layers and the blob instances.

ModelLayer.description: One manifest entry as written, with how the lookup of its blob ended.

BlobLookup.description: How the lookup of a layer's blob ended: NotLookedUp (malformed digest), Found, Absent (confirmed), or Unresolved (unknown).

LicenseText.description: What was read from the license layer's blob.

FileInstance.description: A placement of contents at a path, observed once.

NsInode.description: A namespace's inode, or why it could not be read.

Listener.description: A listening socket in SIGIL's network namespace. Its bind class is derived from the address, never stored.

ListenerOwner.description: Who holds the socket, as far as the readable fd tables show. Never by port.

MappingObs.description: One mapping in one process at one instant. Says nothing about why it was mapped or whether it was used.

Basis.description: How a fact was obtained. Modeled is not 'confirmed in the target': it may assert what the named rule support records, and no more than the fact's own unresolved premises allow.

EvidenceRef.description: A typed pointer to evidence in the session.

Support.description: What supports a behavior claim about a specific artifact. Categories, not ranks. Recorded only in RuleSupport. FeatureMatch never supports a finding condition.

Tri_CandidateWhy.description: A fact: established, refuted, or unknown, with its basis and unresolved premises.

Tri_EffectWhy.description: A fact: established, refuted, or unknown, with its basis and unresolved premises.

Tri_Unit.description: A fact: established, refuted, or unknown, with its basis and unresolved premises.

ComponentClaim.description: Level A. Every source of identity is kept; conflicts coexist.

ReleaseClaim.description: Release identity: always a set; only reference matches close it.

FeatureHint.description: Level B: a feature signal exists. Never 'it is called'.

CodeFacts.description: Level C: code facts of one slice.

Relation.description: Declared, candidate, and symbol-candidate relations are never resolutions; a binding is a BindingPremise.

RuleSupport.description: The support of one profile rule on one slice: the only place a Support is recorded. (profile, rule, slice) is unique.

LoadFacts.description: Independent facts, not a state machine. There is no 'loaded' flag; an empty `mapped` never means 'not loaded'.

ValueOrigin.description: Where a value came from. A configured value is never the effective value.

CoverageState.description: Only Complete, NotPresent, and OutOfScope can close a check; every other state is a gap.

CondEvidence.description: Evidence for a condition: the record that decides it, by kind. Never a copy of the record's conclusion; what it settles is read from the record under its kind's sufficiency rule.

Finding.description: Level E: a dangerous configuration established on every condition. Policy never changes it; `decision` is separate.

OpenQuestion.description: A rule whose conditions are not all established and none refuted. Not a finding.

Outcome.description: Verdict and completeness: independent, always reported together.
